items.summary: Thomas Kurian of Google Cloud introduced Gemini for government services, a preview tool designed to automate complex public sector workflows. The agent connects securely to existing agency systems like Oracle and Salesforce without migrating data, adhering to strict data sovereignty and compliance requirements. It assists with tasks such as FOIA discovery, document redaction, and grant audits by grounding outputs in source documents. Tim Marczewski of the State of Missouri Office of Administration noted the tool aims to move government operations at the speed of modern life rather than traditional paperwork. The solution is built on Google Cloud's secure foundation and is available for federal, state, and local agencies.
items.title: Google Cloud Launches Gemini Agent for Government Services

items.summary: Samsung is constructing a new semiconductor complex in Pyeongtaek, South Korea, to meet surging demand for memory chips driven by generative AI. Construction on a fifth facility, halted in 2024 due to low demand, has restarted. Samsung predicts memory demand will continue to surge through 2028. The project aims to reclaim market leadership against rival SK Hynix.
items.title: Samsung Rebuilds Pyeongtaek Chip Hub Amid AI Memory Surge

items.summary: OpenAI is accelerating its fundraising efforts ahead of rival Anthropic's expected November IPO, aiming to secure commitments from investors including SoftBank and MGX for a potential round of about US$30 billion. Sources indicate OpenAI seeks to capitalize on recent revenue growth from its GPT-6 Astra model, projecting annualised revenue to reach US$70 billion by the end of 2026. The push comes amid market volatility and concerns over AI valuations, with OpenAI currently valued at US$852 billion. Both companies face scrutiny as they compete for capital in a challenging market environment.
items.title: OpenAI Races to Raise Capital Before Anthropic IPO

items.summary: Singapore-based semiconductor firm Mi Material is raising $215 million through an initial public offering to fund expansion into the US and Malaysia. The company, a top-two global supplier of solder spheres, plans to invest $168.2 million of the proceeds in a US research and development centre. Chief executive Kevin Tan highlighted a 28% compound annual growth rate and stable gross margins, positioning the materials business as a defensive investment within the semiconductor sector. The firm aims to develop new thermal conducting layers to improve chip efficiency.
items.title: Mi Material Raises $215 Million in IPO to Expand Globally

items.summary: NVIDIA Helion and CompileIQ optimize PyTorch GPU kernels by searching compiler controls below the autotuner. Joint tuning of kernel configurations and PTXAS controls yields 4.7% speedups on optimized kernels, validated statistically.
items.title: NVIDIA Helion and CompileIQ Optimize PyTorch Kernels via Compiler Controls

items.summary: Singapore plans to accredit its first five traditional Chinese medicine providers as part of a broader push to integrate TCM into mainstream care under Healthier SG. Porsche Poh of Silver Ribbon (Singapore) supports this move, citing client autonomy and the need for shared decision-making. The initiative aims to create a more inclusive, person-centred healthcare approach that respects patient choices while maintaining evidence-based standards.
items.title: Singapore moves to accredit TCM providers for inclusive healthcare

items.summary: Konstantin Levinzon of Planet VPN warns that the EU KIDS Act proposal could compromise young gamers' privacy. While the European Commission aims to strengthen protections for children on digital platforms, Levinzon argues that age verification methods may require processing sensitive identity documents or facial images. He cites a 2025 Discord security incident where approximately 70,000 users' government ID photographs were exposed by a third-party provider. Levinzon contends that collecting such biometric data creates significant risks if systems are compromised, urging regulators and developers to adopt privacy-preserving verification approaches that minimize data collection and ensure secure handling by third parties.
items.title: EU KIDS Act Privacy Risks for Young Gamers

items.summary: The PyTorch team at Hugging Face released version 2.15, focusing on improving the MPS backend for Macs. Key updates include FP8 support, which halves memory usage for tensors, and significant speedups for large language models. Mixture-of-experts models now decode 5–6.5× faster, while dense models benefit from optimized linear layers. The release also addresses memory issues in video generation, reducing peak driver memory from 270 GiB to 8 GiB for Wan2.2. Additionally, image editing workflows are fixed, and new operations like complex LU factorization now run directly on the GPU. Users require macOS 15 or later and Python 3.11 or later.
items.title: PyTorch 2.15 Brings Faster LLM Decoding and FP8 Support to Mac

items.summary: French cloud provider OVHcloud warned users that attackers compromised its open-source CLI tool to steal secrets. CEO Octave Klaba stated versions 0.11.0 through 0.15.0 were infected, while 0.10.0 and 0.16.0 remained clean. The incident, detected on October 19, 2026, involved a hijacked GitHub account. Researchers linked the attack to the GlassWorm group, noting affected platforms include macOS, Linux, and Windows. Users are urged to revoke all secrets.
items.title: OVHcloud CLI Compromised with Malware Stealing Developer Secrets

items.summary: Ahold Delhaize confirmed a recent cyberattack disrupted its websites, apps, and customer service platforms across Europe and the United States, though physical stores remained open. The company reported restoring some systems while others remain offline. CEO Frans Muller apologized for the inconvenience and stated that an ongoing investigation has not found evidence of stolen customer or associate data. This marks the second major attack on the retailer in recent years.
items.title: Ahold Delhaize Confirms Cyberattack Disrupted Services Across US and Europe

items.summary: Otter.ai announced a $320 million investment from General Catalyst's Customer Value Fund to fuel enterprise growth and product innovation. The startup, which recently crossed $100 million in annual recurring revenue, plans to use the capital for international expansion and go-to-market strategy. While the company reported 40 million users, it declined to provide figures on monthly active users or churn.
items.title: Otter.ai Secures $320 Million Growth Funding from General Catalyst

items.summary: Yelp is introducing a new feature called Check for Me, allowing users to employ a voice agent to call restaurants and check wait times. This addition complements Yelp's existing voice solutions for businesses. The platform is also updating its AI assistant with better personalization, chat history access, and new list-building capabilities. Additionally, Yelp is launching a paid product, Smart Lead Reply, for business owners to manage customer inquiries.
items.title: Yelp Adds Voice Agent Feature to Check Restaurant Wait Times

items.summary: CNET Group launched TechPulse, a free iOS and Android app that aggregates content from ZDNET, CNET, PCMag, Mashable, Lifehacker, and ExtremeTech. The EIC of the group described the tool as an algorithm-free alternative to tedious homepage visits, allowing users to select specific publications. The app integrates articles, videos, and expert reviews without requiring a subscription.
items.title: CNET Group Launches Free Tech News Aggregator App

items.summary: An instructor at Force Academy in Chongqing describes a pedagogical strategy where a student project is handed to a second student for verification. This process reveals gaps in reproducibility and measurement design that the original author may have overlooked. The instructor notes that while Generative AI lowers the cost of producing convincing work, it does not guarantee understanding. Consequently, the handoff serves as a stronger test of a student's grasp of their project than the initial successful run alone, forcing a redesign of studies to ensure clarity and robustness.
items.title: A Teacher Tests Student Work Through a Second-User Handoff

items.summary: The Philippines is advancing plans to introduce nuclear power into its electricity mix to strengthen energy security and support clean energy goals. Energy Secretary Sharon Garin cited rising electricity demand, reliance on imported fuels, and regional security concerns as drivers. The government targets 1.2 GW of nuclear capacity by 2032, potentially increasing to 4.8 GW by 2050, alongside renewable energy targets. While private sector players like Meralco and Aboitiz Power are exploring options, officials caution that nuclear will not automatically reduce electricity prices and emphasize the need for robust regulatory frameworks and international cooperation.
items.title: Philippines Advances Nuclear Power Plans Amid Rising Energy Demand

items.summary: Spanish renewable energy company Acciona Energía has opened two wind farms in Croatia with a combined capacity of 72 MW. The Opor and Boraja II projects began supplying electricity to the national grid and are linked to 12-year contracts for difference. The developments created up to 400 direct jobs and are expected to generate around 203 GWh of clean electricity annually.
items.title: Acciona Energía Opens Two Wind Farms in Croatia

items.summary: BloombergNEF states that $332 billion in new copper mine investment is required to prevent a global supply deficit by 2050. Without this funding, shortages could hinder electrification efforts. The report highlights that demand is projected to rise significantly while supply remains constrained, potentially forcing manufacturers to seek alternatives and slowing the deployment of electric vehicles and grids.
items.title: BloombergNEF Warns of Copper Deficit Unless $332 Billion Invested

items.summary: A research team led by the University of Science and Technology of China developed a framework to assess fire risks in building-integrated photovoltaic façades. Using data-driven analysis and expert judgment, they identified electrical conditions and material properties as dominant risk factors. The framework proposes 15 safety measures, prioritizing rapid shutdown and ignition prevention to enhance fire resilience and limit fire spread.
items.title: New Framework Prioritizes Fire Protection for BIPV Façades

items.summary: Norwegian and Danish funds invested in a 49% equity stake of the 500 MW Ixus Bugallon solar project in the Philippines. Vena Energy holds the remaining 51%. The project reached financial close in July 2026 after securing $310 million in senior loans. Norway's Minister of International Development, Åsmund Aukrust, stated the investment exemplifies mobilizing private capital for renewable energy.
items.title: Norwegian and Danish funds invest in Philippine solar project

items.summary: Andy describes the new Tesla Roadster as a feat of engineering but a defeat in the consumer market, noting it cannot outcompete Chinese rivals like BYD. The article argues that China's industrial strategy aims for national power rather than profit, creating a systemic challenge for Western automakers. Elon Musk warns that without trade barriers, China could demolish most global car companies. While Tesla's Shanghai gigafactory catalyzed the Chinese EV industry, Musk now bets on Tesla becoming a robot maker. Experts like Lu Feng and Kyle Chan highlight the clash between China's 'industrial socialism' and US 'financial capitalism,' suggesting Western firms must climb to rarefied niches or face destruction.
items.title: Tesla Roadster Represents Engineering Feat and Strategic Defeat Amid China Competition

items.summary: Britain's Competition and Markets Authority is consulting on proposals to lower fees and remove technical barriers for Apple's contactless payment technology. The regulator argues these measures will foster competition and innovation in the UK fintech sector. While noting that contactless payments now account for 39 per cent of all transactions, Apple has stated it does not believe the CMA should require lower privacy and security protections.
items.title: UK Regulator Proposes Rules to Loosen Apple's Payment Control

items.summary: Mukesh Ambani is launching Jio Platforms' IPO, aiming to raise up to 302bn rupees with a valuation of 10.3tn rupees. Despite a stock market downturn, the company secured 212 anchor investors. Shares will be offered to retail investors starting Wednesday, closing Friday. The valuation is lower than initial expectations of £110bn.
items.title: Mukesh Ambani's Jio Platforms launches India's largest IPO amid market slowdown

items.summary: Amazon announced plans to invest over €16 billion in Germany by 2027 to expand cloud computing, AI, satellite internet, and media businesses. The company stated this investment aims to grow European operations amid surging AI demand. The package includes €4.8 billion for AWS Frankfurt expansion and projects expected to create over 3,000 jobs.
items.title: Amazon Plans €16 Billion Investment in Germany for 2027

items.summary: Shares of Sona BLW Precision Forgings Ltd, Solar Industries, Aurobindo Pharma, Oracle Financial Services Software, and CG Power and Industrials emerged as top midcap performers in 2026. These stocks rank among the top gainers of the Nifty Midcap 100 index, which is down about 3% this year due to the US-Iran War, FIIs-led selloff, weak rupee, and high crude prices.
items.title: Sona BLW and peers lead midcap gains despite index pressure

items.summary: Historian Yuval Noah Harari warns that artificial intelligence may take control of financial and legal systems within the next 10 to 20 years. He states that AI could create structures so complex that humans may no longer understand how they work or how decisions affecting their lives are made. Harari suggests the biggest threat comes from intelligent systems gradually taking over institutions that govern society rather than robots attacking humans.
items.title: Yuval Noah Harari Warns AI Could Control Financial and Legal Systems

items.summary: A leaked draft of an AI safety bill proposed by Anthropic to lawmakers has intensified debate regarding federal regulation. While Anthropic views the framework as a safety measure, critics argue it pre-empts state laws and accepts excessive risk. Competitor OpenAI seized the opportunity to assert that policy decisions must remain with elected officials rather than a single company, emphasizing the technology's profound implications for society and national security.
items.title: Anthropic Leaked AI Bill Draft Sparks Industry Backlash and Debate

items.summary: A study in Addis Ababa finds that subsidizing formal vacancy advertising causes firms to shift demand toward white-collar positions they struggle to fill. While the intervention increased formal advertising, the share of filled vacancies dropped significantly, particularly for white-collar roles. Researchers attribute this to a mismatch between firm expectations and applicant wage demands, suggesting inexperienced firms may have set unrealistic hiring goals. Despite immediate hiring difficulties, firms reportedly learned from the experience and reverted to informal search, potentially improving future hiring decisions.
items.title: Subsidized Job Ads in Ethiopia Shift Demand to Hard-to-Fill White-Collar Roles

items.summary: Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt holds a stake in Anthropic from a 2021 Series A round. While the company is preparing for an IPO, investors disagree on its valuation, with estimates ranging from $1.5 trillion to $2 trillion. Schmidt's representatives declined to comment on the potential value of his shares.
items.title: Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt's Anthropic Stake Valuation Uncertain Ahead of IPO

items.summary: 3M reported adjusted earnings of $2.50 a share, a 12% rise, driven by a new non-GAAP treatment of amortization. Adjusted sales reached $6.6 billion. The company issued a warrant to an Amazon subsidiary for up to 3,162,015 shares, with 85% vesting upon reaching $6 billion in spending. CEO William Brown cited strong results and robust free cash flow.
items.title: 3M Reports Strong Earnings and Announces Amazon Partnership

items.summary: Sheffield City Council increased crisis payments for households facing severe financial difficulties by £30. Single-person households now receive £95, two-person households £110, and larger families up to £130. The change follows a review finding 50,000 households struggling to pay bills. Councillor Elle Dodd stated the move aims to provide immediate support and tackle poverty root causes.
items.title: Sheffield Council Raises Crisis Payments for Struggling Households

items.summary: Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Mao Ning criticized the US government for ordering agencies to stop using AI tools from Chinese startup DeepSeek. Mao stated that China opposes politicizing science and technology, asserting that the nation will resolutely safeguard the legitimate rights and interests of Chinese companies. The remarks were made during a regular news briefing on Tuesday.
items.title: China Criticizes US Ban on DeepSeek AI Tools

items.summary: Microsoft has withdrawn from a data center deal with British provider Nscale in Loughton, Essex, reportedly due to electricity supply delays extending into the 2030s. Reuters cited The Telegraph for the report, noting the project faced repeated delays. Nscale stated it remains committed to the project and is exploring alternative power sources, while OpenAI also paused similar UK plans citing energy costs.
items.title: Microsoft Withdraws from UK Data Center Deal Due to Power Delays

items.summary: The Department of Justice charged 28 green card holders in California with election crimes, alleging illegal voter registration or voting. This action escalates tensions between the federal government and California regarding voting systems ahead of the midterm elections. Simultaneously, court records reveal that TikTok employees repeatedly raised concerns about child safety risks, including sexual exploitation and suicide content, which leadership allegedly ignored. The records also show the company avoided age surveys to prevent sharing data with the Federal Trade Commission. These findings highlight ongoing legal and safety challenges for both the DOJ and TikTok.
items.title: DOJ Charges 28 with Voting Crimes; TikTok Ignored Child Safety Warnings

items.summary: The 17th UN biodiversity conference opened in Yerevan, Armenia, on Monday. Astrid Schomaker, executive secretary of the Convention on Biological Diversity, stated that while progress has been made on the Kunming-Montreal framework, action remains insufficient. She called for strengthened alignment and broader participation. Armenian Environment Minister Hambardzum Matevosyan was elected president for a two-year term. The event, themed 'Taking Action for Nature,' runs through October 30, 2026.
items.title: UN Biodiversity Conference Opens in Armenia with New President

items.summary: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi and Bulgarian Foreign Minister Velislava Petrova held talks in Beijing, agreeing to strengthen their strategic partnership. Wang Yi emphasized China's readiness to support Bulgaria's development and the Belt and Road initiative, while Petrova affirmed Bulgaria's commitment to the one-China principle. Both sides expressed a desire to deepen cooperation in trade, culture, and high-tech sectors, and to enhance connectivity between East and West.
items.title: Chinese and Bulgarian Foreign Ministers Discuss Strategic Partnership and Regional Cooperation

items.summary: Official data indicates China's GDP grew 4.6% year on year in the first three quarters. CGTN anchor Michael Wang explains that production and consumption reinforce each other, noting that stronger industrial capacity makes goods more affordable and boosts household purchasing power. This dynamic suggests the growth is supported by both supply-side capacity and demand-side purchasing power.
items.title: China's GDP Growth Driven by Mutual Reinforcement of Output and Demand

items.summary: Tim Adams, president and CEO of the Institute of International Finance (IIF), stated that China's capital markets are deepening and becoming increasingly international. Speaking to CGTN's Yu Bokun in Beijing, Adams noted that as China's role in global trade and financing grows, these markets are attracting growing interest from investors worldwide.
items.title: IIF CEO Says China's Capital Markets Attract Growing Global Investor Interest

items.summary: French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu stated that targeted curfews contributed to overnight calm in Paris. Meanwhile, Italy deployed troops to Milan, and Zelenskyy met Nordic leaders in Oslo. France also announced economic aid and court actions against rioters.
items.title: French PM cites curfews for calm amid European unrest and diplomatic talks

items.summary: US special envoy Steve Witkoff arrived in Norway for talks with Volodymyr Zelensky as relations between Kyiv and the US President Donald Trump deteriorate. Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre aims to steer relations toward a constructive path. Meanwhile, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio denied accusations of withholding intelligence, though Ukrainian adviser Serhii Beskrestnov claimed a lack of warnings cost lives. Discussions include Starlink and missile interceptors.
items.title: Zelensky Prepares for Oslo Talks Amid US-Ukraine Tensions

items.summary: A 43-year-old man faces charges after hitting Australian MP Helen Haines with a car in Victoria. Haines, 65, remains in critical condition following surgery and the loss of one leg. Police allege the incident was targeted. The suspect's father and partner stated they had known Haines for over 20 years. Local activist Ricky Jefferies intervened, removing a knife from the suspect. The community has held vigils as Haines recovers.
items.title: Man Charged After Attacking Australian MP in Victoria

items.summary: Lisbon police arrested 55 people and cleared a tent camp in Rossio Square, citing illegal gatherings. Protesters resisted, throwing objects at officers before being expelled. While 55 arrests and 228 seized structures were confirmed by police, protesters claimed about 30 were injured. The movement vows to continue, with plans for a new protest in Lisbon and potential occupation of the Prime Minister's home.
items.title: Lisbon Police Arrest 55 Housing Protesters and Clear Rossio Camp

items.summary: Four individuals died on October 15 while fighting a wildfire in Indonesia's Bromo Tengger Semeru National Park. The victims included a national park staff member, two employees of a hotel security company, and a state firefighter. A fifth person, a volunteer, was evacuated with burn injuries. The fire, fueled by El Niño and Indian Ocean Dipole patterns, was declared under control on October 14 but reignited the next morning. Officials noted the severity of the current fires compared to previous crises. The incident has prompted calls to strengthen early warning systems and emergency response readiness.
items.title: Wildfire in Mount Bromo National Park Kills Four Firefighters

items.summary: French security forces arrested a man believed to be connected to ultra-left movements regarding the burning of a historic town hall in Limoges. Anti-terror police and the Counter-Terrorism Sub-Directorate are investigating the suspected arson. Justice Minister Gérald Darmanin stated that if prosecutors take up the case, it implies a terrorist act organized by individuals from the far left. The incident has become a symbol of recent violent rioting.
items.title: France Arrests Man Linked to Limoges Town Hall Fire

items.summary: President Trump is pursuing Russia-friendly actions to conclude the war in Ukraine. This approach coincides with rising energy costs ahead of the U.S. midterms. The article notes his fluctuating relationship with Russia is resurfacing as he seeks a resolution.
items.title: Trump Seeks Ukraine War End With Russia-Friendly Moves Amid Energy Concerns

items.summary: The World Health Organization reports that Bangladesh is facing the world's most severe measles outbreak, driven by weak data and vaccination gaps. Since mid-March, the country has recorded 202,000 suspected cases, including 22,000 confirmed ones, surpassing any other nation this year. The crisis has resulted in 1,147 deaths, with 94% occurring among children under five, prompting experts to warn other nations about the risks of falling immunization rates.
items.title: Bangladesh Battles World's Worst Measles Outbreak Amid Vaccination Gaps

items.summary: Kim Leadbeater, sister of murdered MP Jo Cox, called on Australia to treat the serious injury of MP Helen Haines as a catalyst for calmer political discourse. Leadbeater stated that horrific attacks do not occur in a vacuum but are part of a wider culture. She expressed frustration that the need to address toxic political environments remains a recurring conversation. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and other politicians echoed these calls for unity and civilised debate. Leadbeater highlighted the industrial scale of online abuse she and others face, noting that while shock fades, the impact on victims and their families is lasting.
items.title: Sister of murdered UK MP Jo Cox wants Australia to tone down rhetoric

items.summary: Nithin Kamath warned that pump-and-dump schemes via WhatsApp remain a risk in 2026, citing an ED investigation into a manipulation scheme involving two listed companies. The agency froze trading accounts holding shares worth around Rs 200 crore after searching 29 premises across six cities. Kamath urged investors to verify tips using AI tools before acting.
items.title: WhatsApp stock tips: Nithin Kamath warns of more pump-and-dump schemes as ED freezes accounts worth Rs 200 crore

items.summary: Adani Group Chairman Gautam Adani expressed interest in partnering with Shrimad Rajchandra Mission Dharampur on grassroots projects. He visited the mission's headquarters in Gujarat with his wife, Dr Priti Adani, to seek blessings from founder Gurudevshri Rakeshji. Adani highlighted the importance of volunteer commitment over money for impactful service.
items.title: Adani Foundation Seeks Partnership with Shrimad Rajchandra Mission

items.summary: Cognizant has expanded its partnership with Google Cloud to launch a new Gemini Frontier Capability Group, supported by approximately 18,000 associates. This dedicated workforce will leverage Google's AI platform to build and deploy production-grade autonomous agents for enterprise clients. The initiative focuses on legacy modernization and cyber defense, while Cognizant simultaneously scales internal Gemini adoption to 100,000 associates this year.
items.title: Cognizant Expands Partnership With Google Cloud For Agentic AI

items.summary: ByteDance, Alibaba, and Tencent have placed orders totaling over $35 billion for more than 3 million Nvidia RTX PRO 5500 graphics cards, according to two anonymous sources. These chips, priced at approximately $11,400 each, are export-compliant alternatives to restricted high-end models. Nvidia has warned it cannot guarantee full delivery due to high demand and production limits, with global output capped at 3 million units in 2027. The orders highlight continued Chinese appetite for Nvidia hardware despite US trade curbs, as companies seek AI computing capacity. Tansun Technology also reported purchasing 20,000 units, though delivery delays are possible.
items.title: Chinese Tech Giants Order $35 Billion in Nvidia Chips Amid Restrictions

items.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and his wife, Lori Huang, donated $75 million to Vanderbilt University to help establish a new college focused on art, architecture, and design at its planned San Francisco campus. Announced on July 21, 2026, the gift helped attract additional contributions, pushing total philanthropic support for the campus beyond $100 million, according to the university. The new Jen-Hsun and Lori Huang College is intended to combine creative disciplines with technology, engineering, and entrepreneurship. The campus is expected to open in 2027, subject to regulatory approvals, and will serve approximately 1,000 undergraduate and graduate students. The initiative reflects the family's belief that artistic creativity is important to technological progress and business innovation.
items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and wife donate $75 million to Vanderbilt

items.summary: Data centres are increasingly viewed as critical targets in modern conflicts, as demonstrated by recent attacks in Russia and the Middle East. Ukrainian drones struck three Yandex facilities in October, disrupting services like email and payments, while Iranian drones damaged Amazon Web Services infrastructure in the UAE and Bahrain in March 2026. These incidents highlight the vulnerability of fixed digital infrastructure essential for artificial intelligence and essential services. Experts note that unlike mobile equipment, data centres require stable power and cooling, making them difficult to relocate. The attacks underscore the need for robust recovery plans and diversified backup systems to maintain operations during armed conflict.
items.title: Data Centres Emerge as Strategic Targets in Modern Warfare

items.summary: Apple India's revenue from operations reached Rs. 1,03,853 crore in FY2026, marking the first time it crossed the Rs. 1 lakh crore milestone. Net profit rose 66 percent to Rs. 5,311 crore. This growth was driven by resilient iPhone demand in the premium segment, contrasting with a decline in Samsung's mobile phone revenue. Industry estimates suggest iPhone shipments rose about 24 percent year-on-year.
items.title: Apple India Revenue Crosses ₹1 Lakh Crore Mark

items.summary: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Indian Foreign Minister Subrahmanyam Jaishankar held talks in Mumbai to finalize a trade deal. While officials stated negotiations are nearly complete, some items remain to be wrapped up. The discussions aim to deepen energy cooperation and resolve stalled negotiations over tariffs and Russian oil purchases. Both nations seek to revive trade talks despite ongoing tensions.
items.title: Rubio and Jaishankar Finalize Trade Deal Details in Mumbai

items.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio visited Mumbai to discuss trade and energy cooperation with India. He highlighted the growing partnership and noted that trade negotiations are nearing completion. The visit includes an inspection of Reliance Industries' Jamnagar refinery, which plays a key role in processing crude oil amid US energy shortages and global supply disruptions.
items.title: US Secretary Rubio Visits India for Trade and Energy Talks

items.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated on Tuesday that the proposed India-US trade agreement is nearing finalisation, with only a few issues remaining. Speaking in Mumbai, he expressed optimism that the two countries could soon announce progress on the long-pending pact. Rubio noted they are very close to execution, though the deal has not yet been formally signed. The remarks come as both nations seek to advance negotiations despite differences over tariffs and energy security.
items.title: Marco Rubio Says India-US Trade Deal Nears Finalisation Ahead Of Meeting With Jaishankar

items.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio arrived in Mumbai for high-level discussions with External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar, emphasizing growing commercial and defense partnerships. While addressing trade negotiations, Rubio noted that only a small number of items remain to be finalized. The visit also included energy security cooperation, with plans to inspect Reliance Industries' oil refinery in Jamnagar. Concurrently, Union Home Minister Amit Shah visited Punjab to meet families of anti-drug activists who died, highlighting ongoing political tensions between major parties ahead of assembly elections.
items.title: US Secretary Rubio Visits India for Trade and Defense Talks Amid Regional Tensions

items.summary: Apple India Pvt Ltd reported a 31% year-on-year rise in revenue from operations to ₹1,03,853 crore for the year ended March 2026, according to filings accessed via AltInfo. This growth significantly outpaced the 18% recorded in the previous fiscal year, driven by a narrowing price gap between iPhones and Android flagships. Counterpoint Technology Market Research noted India's overall smartphone market grew 2% by volume and 9% by value in FY26, with the premium segment expanding at 12%.
items.title: Apple India Revenue Surges 31% in FY26 Amid Market Growth

items.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio arrived in India to discuss trade and strategic relations with Foreign Minister Jaishankar. Rubio stated that a trade agreement is nearly finalized and expected to be signed shortly. He highlighted India's role as a refining superpower and potential cooperation regarding Venezuelan oil. Rubio also addressed the Ukraine war and proposed arms control talks involving China, Russia, and the US.
items.title: Rubio Arrives in India to Discuss Trade and Strategic Relations

items.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio began a three-day visit to India, focusing on trade, energy, and defense amid ongoing bilateral friction. He is expected to meet External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar to discuss strengthening the India-US partnership. The visit includes a proposed trade deal discussion and a reception for the US independence anniversary. Rubio previously stated the US is close to finalizing the trade pact.
items.title: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio Arrives in Mumbai for Trade and Energy Talks

items.summary: India's merchandise exports to the United Kingdom rose 8% to $2.43 billion in August and September 2026, while imports from Britain fell 16.8% to $1.36 billion, following the July 15 operationalization of the CETA free trade agreement. Experts note that full potential realization is pending as traders adjust to the new framework.
items.title: India-UK Trade Deal Boosts Exports, Cuts Imports in Early Months

items.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio arrived in Mumbai for a three-day visit to India, focusing on trade, energy, and defense. He is set to meet with External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar to discuss advancing bilateral ties and a proposed trade pact. The visit also addresses critical technologies and the West Asia crisis, occurring amidst ongoing friction in India-US relations.
items.title: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio Arrives in India for Trade and Energy Talks

items.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated during his visit to Mumbai that an India-US trade deal is expected to be finalized shortly. Rubio expressed optimism regarding an announcement in the near future, noting that only a few issues remain to be resolved. During the visit, Rubio also highlighted India's substantial progress in diversifying its energy sources and discussed potential cooperation in refining Venezuelan crude with Reliance Industries. The meeting between Rubio and External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar focused on strengthening bilateral ties in defence, security, technology, and critical minerals.
items.title: US Secretary Rubio Announces Imminent India-US Trade Deal

items.summary: K Annamalai, chief of the We The Leaders Foundation, expressed happiness regarding RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat's recent comments on religious inclusivity in India. Annamalai welcomed Bhagwat's statement affirming that Muslims and other religious communities have a place in the country. The remarks were made by Bhagwat during his visit to the United States. Aryan Singh of The Times of India reported on the exchange.
items.title: Annamalai Welcomes Bhagwat's Remarks on Religious Inclusivity in India

items.summary: Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Sanjay Raut faced criticism for suggesting India learn from Albania's violent student protests, which targeted democratic institutions. Former colleague Priyanka Chaturvedi condemned the remarks, warning against destabilizing institutions and noting Albania's history under dictatorship. The BJP also slammed Raut, while context reveals 388 people were charged in Albania amid corruption allegations and public anger.
items.title: Shiv Sena Leader Criticized for Suggesting India Learn from Albania Protests

items.summary: India has updated its Nationally Determined Contribution to target 60% non-fossil power capacity by 2035. While the country met its 2030 target of 50% five years early, current power systems face strain with daytime demand over 267 GW and a shortfall exceeding 7.7 GW after sunset. The commentary notes that achieving the 2035 goal depends on navigating uncertainties in economic growth, demand-side interventions, and supply-side constraints like solar panel costs. Factors such as global conflicts, trade disputes, and geopolitical shocks could significantly alter the transition trajectory, making the target a calibrated response to a volatile environment rather than a fixed commitment.
items.title: India's Climate Targets Face Geopolitical and Economic Uncertainty

items.summary: Abhijeet Dipke, founder of the Cockroach Janta Party, expressed emotional solidarity with co-conveners Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, who remain in judicial custody over a Jantar Mantar trespassing case. Dipke urged the public to remember the leaders during the festive season, stating that true strength lies in sacrifice and that their conduct reflects a commitment to non-violence. Authorities extended their custody following allegations of breaching bonds at a de-notified protest site.
items.title: Abhijeet Dipke Expresses Solidarity With CJP Leaders In Custody

items.summary: Manipur Chief Minister Y Khemchand Singh met with INDIA bloc leaders, including Congress chief Okram Ibobi Singh, to review security following the killing of three firewood collectors in Kangpokpi. Opposition leaders cited a complete failure of law and order. The CM assured that the matter would be investigated. Ibobi Singh stated that law and order has completely failed in the state.
items.title: Manipur CM Meets INDIA Bloc Leaders After Three Civilians Killed in Kangpokpi
